subject: Request: temporary response guarantee adjustment for nightly ingestion bursts
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@greenfield.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-03T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Nightly ingestion spikes — temporary SLA request

Marcus,

Quick note — over the last three nights our pipeline has produced large ingestion bursts between 02:00–05:00 UTC tied to a nightly enrichment job. That has driven a spike in P2 incidents (majorly degraded inference throughput) and we’re seeing several P2s open inside the 30-minute response window before human routing completes.

Given the volume and the time window, we need to propose a short-term operational change while we roll out a fix on our side next month. Two asks:

- Can Redwood provide dedicated on-call coverage for our 02:00–05:00 UTC window for the next 3 weeks?
- Alternatively, if dedicated coverage isn’t feasible, can we agree to temporarily relax the P2 response guarantee to 60 minutes for that window, and define a clear escalation path for P1s?

I attached a short request summary and some ingestion logs. We opened ticket GL-3245 earlier this morning.

We’re happy to discuss options and compensate for the out-of-hours coverage. Can you confirm what’s possible and the fastest timeline?

Thanks,
Jake Turner
Head of Platform Engineering
Greenfield AI
Attachments: SLA_change_request_v1.pdf, ingestion-logs-20261031.zip
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T19:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nightly ingestion spikes — temporary SLA request

Jake — thanks for the detailed note and the logs. We’ve pulled GL-3245 into our operations queue and ran an initial triage. High level: the P2 volume is concentrated in that 3-hour window and appears tied to a burst of long-running batched jobs that are creating heavy KV cache churn.

Options we can move on quickly (please pick the one you prefer):

A) Dedicated night coverage: Redwood assigns a supplemental on-call engineer for the 02:00–05:00 UTC window for three weeks. This includes a named responder, 30-minute response objective for P2s during that window, and daily handoff notes. There’s an additional nightly labor surcharge; we can circulate a short amendment.

B) Temporary response adjustment: For the next 3 weeks we amend the P2 response objective to 60 minutes only for incidents originating in 02:00–05:00 UTC, with mandatory P1 escalation within 15 minutes and automatic paging to senior on-call if a P2 remains unacknowledged for 90 minutes. We’d pair this with increased telemetry and a canonical runbook for the burst class.

Both options include:
- A shared on-call Slack channel and a daily 10-minute sync until the load stabilizes.
- A one-week retro and a rollback clause if customer-observed impact is higher than expected.

I’ve looped in Ben (CS) and Priyom (support ops) to give numbers on costs and to prepare an amendment doc if you choose A. If you prefer B we can issue a short addendum without a fee and set tighter P1 controls.

Propose a quick call tomorrow to lock the approach.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@greenfield.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nightly ingestion spikes — temporary SLA request

Jake — thanks for flagging and for the logs. From CS perspective I recommend option A if you expect frequent operator intervention; option B if this is purely a throughput/backpressure issue and you want to avoid a recurring surcharge.

If we go with A, we’ll:
- Put an on-call engineer from the Support Night Roster on a three-week supplement (names will be provided today).
- Add a bridged channel and a 4AM UTC checklist to speed diagnosis.
- Provide an amended SLA doc (draft attached).

If B, we’ll still deploy an automated canary route for your traffic during the window and temporarily raise the P2 target to 60 minutes as Marcus suggested. We’ll instrument an alert that escalates to a senior on-call at 60 minutes.

Attached: proposed-sla-amendment-draft.docx (draft of contract amendment + operational checklist).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment-draft.docx
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@greenfield.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Nightly ingestion spikes — temporary SLA request

Thanks Marcus and Ben. After internal discussion we’ll take option A: dedicated night coverage for the 02:00–05:00 UTC window for three weeks. We prefer named ownership and a hard 30-minute P2 objective during that window.

Two quick asks before you spin up the roster:
- Start date: the sooner the better. Can we make the first night 2026-11-06?
- Please include the daily 4AM runbook checklist and a single escalation matrix (who to page at 30 / 60 / 90 minutes).

I attached another zip with the last three nights of ingestion traces for your ops lead. We’ll sign the amendment via DocuSign once we have the draft.

Best,
Jake
Attachments: ingestion-logs-20261031.zip
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@greenfield.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nightly ingestion spikes — temporary SLA request

Jake / team — confirming we’ll provision dedicated supplemental on-call coverage starting 2026-11-06 through 2026-11-26 for 02:00–05:00 UTC. Summary of commitments:

- Coverage: Named supplemental responder assigned nightly (primary + backup).
- Response objective: 30-minute target for P2s during the window; P1 escalation within 15 minutes.
- Escalation path: responder -> senior on-call after 30 minutes -> support manager (Priyom) after 60 minutes -> engineering incident lead after 90 minutes.
- Ops artifacts: 4AM runbook checklist, shared Slack channel #greenfield-night-ops, and daily 1-pager handoff.
- Billing: nightly supplement fee applied; Ben will share the invoice schedule and an amendment doc via DocuSign (link below).

Links:
- JIRA: GL-3245 (internal triage)
- DocuSign amendment (draft): https://docsend.redwood.com/sla-amendment/greenfield
- Incident playbook (read-only): https://app.redwood.com/tickets/GL-3245

We’ll send the roster and the amendment by end of day. If anything changes or you want a different start date, shout.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Support Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
